correctness.rationale: The full normalization is reconstructed from radial Fourier/Sonine integration, the Bessel order is d/2+beta, and the radial exponent after the leading oscillation is -1-(beta-(d-1)/2). Fixed-order Bessel remainder is uniformly integrable near the boundary, and |cos|-2/pi has a bounded phase-uniform primitive; its weighted integral is uniformly O(1). The exact gamma prefactor simplifies to 4 Gamma((d+1)/2)/(pi^(3/2) Gamma(d/2)). Fourier uniqueness of finite measures and Cauchy–Schwarz prove minimum second moment and impossibility when the signed spectrum is not finite. Numerical script independently passed 62 finite checks; those are corroborative, not infinite proof.

value.rationale: The signed random Fourier feature method explicitly requires an L1 spectral density for compactly supported kernels. The theorem gives the exact feasibility threshold, sharp dimensional residue, uniform finite-frequency crossover, diverging negative spectral mass, and unavoidable inverse-square second-moment penalty for the optimal one-frequency estimator in a natural radial subfamily. This changes both the admissibility and expected simulation cost at a motivated boundary, rather than measuring an arbitrary Bessel integral. The class of estimators and scope are explicit.
